To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) absorptive capacity is a process, not an event, 2) absorptive capacity can be enhanced by the development of specific capabilities that allow organizational actors to accept and assimilate external information, 3) absorptive capacity should be viewed as a long-term process that is developed over time, 4) absorptive capacity requires the simultaneous exploration and exploitation of new information, 5) absorptive capacity cannot be fully understood without the development of an organizational culture that supports and encourages learning
absorptive capacity is a dynamic process, which can be described in terms of learning cycles.

the learning process in large-scale IS implementation requires a) the accumulation of knowledge; b) a long-term perspective; and c) phases of explorative learning and exploitative learning which overlap.

the role of organizational learning and absorptive capacity in ERP implementation.
the question of how organizations learn from the implementation of large-scale IS projects.
the development and application of absorptive capacity in a large-scale IS implementation project.

absorptive capacity is a complex and dynamic concept that is not easy to grasp.
the implementation of ERP is not only a one-time process, but rather a process that requires the accumulation of organizational learning and knowledge.

the development of absorptive capacity in ERP implementations requires the development of a) specific organizational capabilities, b) a long-term perspective on learning, and c) a capacity to explore and simultaneously exploit knowledge.
